procedure: Verify all ten input hashes and byte lengths before relying on any input; stop on mismatch.
Run `learn -s "file download batch export hogql"` once (alone), then `info` for file-download-batch-exports-create / -retrieve / -count-rows-create / -cancel-create if not already known.

Use EXACTLY the retained query bytes of literal-projection.hogql (sha 87c47aa6…) as hogql_query; file {format: JSONLines, compression: null, max_size_mb: null}; hogql_modifiers {convertToProjectTimezone: false}; no data_interval bounds (the query has no placeholders).
First call file-download-batch-exports-count-rows-create with the same query and modifiers; retain the response; expected 3. If the count is not 3, stop and report (do not start an export).

Then call file-download-batch-exports-create ONCE. Retain the full response (run id). Poll file-download-batch-exports-retrieve every ~20 s, recording each status with a UTC timestamp, until a terminal status; stop polling after 20 minutes and report. Cancel only if the run exceeds 20 minutes.

On Completed: retain records_completed and the files array (UUIDs). Attempt the REST download ONLY if an authenticated PostHog HTTP context already exists in this environment (check for an environment variable whose NAME contains POSTHOG and a key; do not read connector internals, do not guess keys). If none exists, do not download; record the exact endpoint that needs authentication: GET https://<posthog host>/api/projects/117863/file_download_batch_exports/<run_id>/download/<file_uuid>/ (host as reported by the tools or the skill), the authentication context required, and write the narrow Codex-worker handoff (download each UUID, sha256 and byte length, verify exactly three JSONLines rows with the 21 expected column names from the query, retain files and hashes, no other API call).

If download was possible: save each part under parts/ named posthog-hogql-<run_id>-<part>.jsonl, compute sha256 and bytes, parse JSONLines, verify exactly three rows whose uuid values are the three literal UUIDs of the query and whose keys are exactly the 21 aliases; record any deviation (extra keys, type rendering, ordering).

Write the receipt and run JSON.
